notes:
• Front Desk: the Mac notices when its line to OpenAI stalls or breaks, reconnects, holds actions while it can't hear „Stopp“ and tells you what didn't arrive; the apps show Mac reconnecting… / Reconnecting… and keep the call through network drops of up to 15 s.
• The Front Desk can now approve a plan waiting for approval or send what to change in it, after telling you what the plan says (other blocked actions still stay in the app). A plan that arrives counts as waiting for approval in the Front Desk's queue until it's decided, not as a finished turn, and nothing else goes to that chat by voice meanwhile. The Front Desk can also let an agent fix a failed setup script, like "Fix" in the app. It starts new workspaces on an open pull request or a branch, and with the agent, model, effort or plan mode you ask for (plan mode only with Claude Code). A branch that already has a workspace gets that workspace; a pull request from a fork, a branch that doesn't exist and one checked out outside Stellwerk are refused. It can list a project's open pull requests and branches to start from. "Work on PR" no longer shows a fork's pull request as already having a workspace because its branch has the same name as one of yours. A plan too long to be read whole is approved in the app only (changes still go by voice). Nothing goes by voice to a chat whose agent waits for an answer to its question: the Front Desk answers it or uses a new chat. When checking out an existing branch for a new workspace fails, trying again (by voice or with "Work on PR") checks it out again instead of opening the failed workspace. A branch counts as existing on the remote only under its full name, and searching pull requests and branches by voice also finds older ones.
• Front Desk: news and action results wait for a real pause instead of talking over you; instructions aren't cut off mid-sentence, and „Äh ne, Moment, ich meinte …“ holds what was about to go out.
• Front Desk: ask it to show you a chat ("zeig mir den Chat", "mach den Workspace auf") and it opens that chat on the device the call runs on, on iPhone, iPad, Android and in the Mac window (also one connected to another Mac), as a chat link would: the chat you name, else the one its request is about, else the one active last. The call card goes down to its bar so the chat shows; the Mac opens its Stellwerk window. With the phone locked or the app in the background it opens once the app is in front, and the voice says so. Only the device with the call opens it, and nothing opens again after the call moves to another device, also when the device was locked or offline while it moved. When the device doesn't confirm, the voice says it couldn't confirm the chat opened. Apps from before this can't, and the voice says so; chats of archived workspaces don't open.
• Front Desk: while an agent works, an instruction or question by voice still waits in the chat's queue, but it can now also go right into the running turn, as Send now does in the apps ("schick's ihm sofort", or a correction of what the agent is doing). The voice says which one it does; when it's unclear, it asks "direkt oder in die Warteschlange?". Two messages sent to an idle chat at the same moment no longer start two turns side by side: the second goes into the turn the first started.
• Agents can offer a Google Cloud sign-in in the chat: when gcloud or Google's client libraries need one, the agent's reply shows a "Sign in to Google Cloud" button on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android. One sign-in renews both the gcloud CLI and the client libraries, from whatever device you're on: copy the code Google shows and come back, and Stellwerk takes it from the clipboard and finishes (in the window on the Mac that runs the agents there's no code at all). Afterwards it tells the chat, so the agent carries on by itself. The Mac window's Settings → Account now shows the Mac's Google Cloud sign-ins too, with Sign in and Renew.
• Mac: right-click a file or folder in All files, or a file in Changes, for Conductor's menu: Open in (Finder, editors, terminals; 1–9 pick the first nine), Copy path and Copy relative path. Changes adds View and Discard changes, which puts the file back to how it is on the target branch (a new one goes into the Trash) after asking. Open in also knows Rider and PhpStorm.
• Sections in the project list: group projects into your own sections such as "Work" and "Private", each with an optional emoji and a header in small caps that a click folds. Projects in no section stay on top as before, so nothing changes without sections. On the Mac, a section's ⋯ (on hover) or right-click adds a project to it and makes, edits or deletes sections; "New Section…" is also in "Add Project", in a right-click on the sidebar and in a project's "Move to Section". Projects and sections are dragged into place. iPhone, iPad and Android show and fold the sections and move projects with "Move to Section" in a project's long-press menu.
• The Operator is gone: no more Operator row, to-do list or chat on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android, and no Settings → Operator page. The Front Desk row now sits at the top of the list. Hosts tell older apps the Operator is off, so they hide it too.
• `stellwerk://workspace/<id>` opens a workspace with its last chat on whichever paired Mac has it, on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android, the way `stellwerk://chat/<id>` opens a chat. An optional `session=<chat id>` opens it on that chat (a closed one comes back as a tab), so Conductor's `workspace?id=…&session=…` form works too. Agents know the id as `$STELLWERK_WORKSPACE_ID`, so a task board can link to where an agent works on a task. An archived workspace isn't restored by the link: the app says it's archived on that Mac.
• The pills over the message box (subagents, background commands, wakeups) wrap onto more lines when there are many, instead of running off the side, on the Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android.
• Front Desk: Settings → Front Desk → Longest call also offers 2 and 4 hours, beside 10 to 60 minutes. The default stays 20 minutes; the voice still wraps up a minute before the limit.
• Front Desk: the voice no longer reads out the brain's notes, and the brain corrects what the voice promised before its answer.
• Mac: during a Front Desk call, pressing the AirPods' stem (or a Beats' button) mutes and unmutes the microphone, like the call window's Mute. The iPhone already does this through CallKit; Android has no such gesture for apps. Hanging up by pressing twice isn't possible on the Mac (macOS brings up Siri instead).
• Mac: the right panel's Changes, All files and Checks tabs are always there, in that order. They no longer close (the × that came up on hover covered the end of the tab's title or count), and the "+" for reopening them is gone.
• A question the agent asks while starting a background subagent (or making another call at the same time) no longer disappears: the chat keeps waiting for your answer instead of showing "working" forever. Writing a message instead of answering a question now reaches the agent: the question is turned down and the message goes into the running turn, for Claude Code, Codex and Pi.
